text: A 2019 engineering account describes reducing three MongoDB collections from individually provisioned throughput to shared database throughput, then encountering shard-key requirements and import throttling. Its practical lesson is to test collection layout and migration traffic as part of sizing; its historical minimum-throughput figures should not be reused as current prices. (low confidence)

text: Inspect explain execution statistics when a query is expensive: compare retrievedDocumentCount with outputDocumentCount, inspect pathsNotIndexed, and inspect shardInformation. Microsoft documents partition-key equality filters as reducing query fan-out and RU consumption. A historical count-query trace demonstrates that an indexed-looking query can still retrieve many documents and incur high RU. (high confidence)
keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads

text: Adiom recommends testing query and write performance under expected load and reviewing indexes when moving between MongoDB-compatible implementations. keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads

text: Use the measured workload mix to estimate RU/s: sum each operation class's measured RU charge multiplied by its operations per second. text: For workload sizing, measure request charge on representative MongoDB operations before projecting throughput. RU abstracts CPU, I/O and memory consumption; it is not a fixed price per MongoDB command. Microsoft recommends obtaining query RU charge before optimization. (high confidence)

text: The MongoDB estimator maps find to Reads, insert to Writes, update to Updates, delete to Deletes, and aggregate/query to Queries. text: Microsoft gives Provisioned RU/s = C*T/R as a rough starting estimate, with C=1000 RU/s per vCore for Cosmos DB for MongoDB v4.0, T the total cores across data-bearing replicas, and R the replication factor. Exclude routing/configuration cores; check whether a managed service reports cores per replica before calculating T. This is not a version-independent benchmark or guaranteed equivalence. text: Query partition targeting affects RU demand: an equality filter on the partition key limits index work to the relevant partition, whereas indexed cross-partition queries still execute independently on multiple partitions. Include actual shard-key access patterns in the estimate. (low confidence)
keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads

text: Budget bulk ingestion separately from steady-state traffic and validate it under load. Adiom identifies large ingestion and scan-heavy workloads as provisioning risks; an independent MongoDB-API demo account reported import throttling at its low steady-state allocation and successful import after a temporary increase. These accounts do not supply a universal RU-per-write constant. (medium confidence)
